content.intro: In this lesson, you will study optional values with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you compose readable data transformations and understand when stream operations execute. In this lesson, focus on optional and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A stream pipeline describes transformations over a source. Intermediate operations are lazy; a terminal operation triggers work, and stream instances should not be reused after a terminal operation. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

items.title: OptionalInt and related types
items.text: Primitive variables store values of the eight primitive types. Choose a type that represents the domain and range required; use exact decimal arithmetic for monetary values when appropriate.

items.title: map() and flatMap()
items.text: Choose a collection according to ordering, uniqueness, lookup, and update requirements. Review equals/hashCode contracts, iteration behavior, and concurrent-modification rules before selecting an implementation.

items.title: Avoiding careless calls to get()
items.text: A stream pipeline expresses transformations over a source. Intermediate operations are lazy, a terminal operation triggers processing, and a stream should not be reused after it is consumed. Apply that reasoning specifically to avoiding careless calls to get() and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test.

CodeLeaf does not execute Java in the browser; use a local JDK for these examples. Preview-only and configuration-file examples have their own version or filename notes.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, remove any temporary output files it created, and rerun the baseline case. Do not leave credentials, generated private data, or large test files in the project directory.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.
